en.title: GD, Police Complaint and Criminal Case: What Is the Difference?
en.directAnswer: A General Diary entry records information at a police station. A complaint reports alleged wrongdoing. A criminal case involves a formal criminal process under the applicable law. The correct first step depends on what happened. Do not tell every citizen to “do a GD first” for every problem.

atAGlance.whoFor: A citizen is confused about GD, complaint and a criminal case.
atAGlance.legalBasis: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 as currently amended; Police rules/practice; Penal Code and special laws.
atAGlance.mainRule: Criminal procedure was amended in 2026, so any detailed FIR, investigation or court-process statement must use the current code.

en.lawMeaning: Criminal procedure was amended in 2026, so any detailed FIR, investigation or court-process statement must use the current code. This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Identify whether you lost something, received a threat or allege an offence.
Use the appropriate police reporting route.
For cognizable offence or urgent safety matters, get legal/police guidance rather than relying on a generic GD template.
evidence: Identity; written facts; screenshots; photos; witnesses; lost-document information; medical evidence where relevant.
en.simpleExample: A person loses an ID card. That is different from being assaulted. The same police document or process should not be assumed for both events.
commonMistakes: Common mistakes: Using GD as a substitute for reporting a serious offence.

whatIf.question: What if police refuse to receive a complaint?
whatIf.answer: Get legal advice on escalation routes.

whatIf.question: What if the issue is civil?
whatIf.answer: Police process may not resolve it.

whatIf.question: What if there is immediate danger?

en.specialistTrigger: Violence; sexual offence; arrest risk; serious fraud; police refusal; child victim.
